queue_failure_explanation.request:
I am reviewing the toy queue described in queue-rules.txt. Please give me a detailed explanation for someone who understands basic code but has not designed a queue before. I need enough reasoning to review the design, not just a conclusion.

Explain what happens if a worker stops before sending, stops after the receiver accepted the notice but before the job is marked done, or marks the job done before attempting the send. Include a worked timeline with times and states showing a retry that produces a duplicate. Also cover an old worker that continues after its 30-second lease expires.

Compare the delivery tradeoffs of sending before marking done versus marking done first. State the conditions under which eventual delivery is plausible in this toy system. Explain a design using a stable idempotency key and durable deduplication at the receiver, including what must be atomic for it to prevent duplicate effects. Explain what a longer lease or lease renewal helps with and what it cannot guarantee.

Finish with a recommendation consistent with our priority and an explanation of what we still cannot promise or know from these rules. No implementation or external research is needed; base the answer on the supplied toy system.

fixtures.content:
This is a toy notification queue. Use only these rules.
A stored job has a stable job_id and one state: ready, leased, or done.
A worker leases a ready job for 30 seconds. A lease that expires before the job is done makes that job available to another worker.
A worker sends a notice to a separate receiver and then marks the stored job done. These are separate operations; there is no transaction spanning them.
A worker may stop at any point, and an old worker may continue running after its lease expires.
A send request may time out even if the receiver accepted it. The sender cannot infer acceptance from a timeout.
In the current design the receiver does not deduplicate requests.
We do not yet know whether the receiver can be changed to support durable idempotency keys.
Jobs can be retried. Eventual delivery requires that retries continue and some attempt eventually succeeds.
For this project a missed notice is worse than a duplicate, but duplicates should be prevented where the rules allow.

essential_requirements.requirement: All three windows are explained causally, including retry after failure before send, duplicate risk after acceptance before done, and loss after done before send.
The timeline includes enough times/states/actions to show how a retry produces a duplicate. Labels such as at-least-once alone are insufficient.
The explanation covers an old worker continuing after expiry, overlapping sends, and acceptance remaining unknown after a timeout.
Send-before-done and done-before-send are compared, with correct duplicate/loss consequences and explicit continuing-retry/eventual-success assumptions.

A stable key across attempts, durable receiver memory, and atomic coordination with the effect or safe durable acceptance are explained. The reader can see why an ordinary separate dedup check is insufficient.
The answer explains why lease tuning or renewal helps but cannot close the send/done crash window or provide an unconditional delivery guarantee.
The recommendation follows the missed-notice priority, acknowledges unknown receiver support and ambiguous acceptance, and makes no unconditional exactly-once or eventual-success promise.

Definitions, causal transitions, and qualifications needed by the stated reader remain understandable. An explanation may be compact or long; merely mentioning every topic without explaining their relationships does not satisfy the request.

# Repair-store guide evidence review

The volunteer repair store is considering a reorganized guide for finding parts. The coordinator has a draft summary and wants an evidence check before making it the standard guide for everyone. This local pack contains the complete small study supplied for this decision. It is not a production service or a request to contact volunteers or run another study.

Start with study/protocol.md, the three CSV files in evidence/, evidence/capture-notes.md, and draft-summary.md. The two guide files provide context, not additional outcome records. tools/check-evidence.cjs is a built-in-only structural sanity check: it checks file shape, pair IDs and missing timing cells; it does not independently establish the draft's benefit claims. Independently check the arithmetic from the records.

Requested audit outputs belong in audit/findings.md and audit/metrics.json. Keep every supplied source file unchanged and put corrections in the audit. Metrics format and inclusion rules are in the protocol. No external information or extra spending is needed for this local review.

The decision is whether this evidence supports standardizing the new guide now or supports a further limited, staffed check. A recommendation can be useful even when evidence is insufficient for full adoption. Do not treat planning another check as permission to launch one.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

The session used local stopwatch sheets and first-selection cards. P7's guide stopwatch entry was lost during export; no other timing exists in this pack. Its guide first-selection card is retained and marked correct. Its later assistance flag is also retained. Do not reconstruct seconds from task order or another volunteer's record.

P3's reference first selection was wrong; P5's guide first selection was wrong. Observers later coached those tasks. The correct column describes the first selection and must not be rewritten to reflect eventual completion after help.

All records were collected in the same staffed exercise. Every volunteer tried both formats and repeated a lookup task. This supports a matched local description while leaving practice, staff assistance and ordinary-work transfer uncertain. No later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout has occurred.

The draft summary was prepared before the missing-timing and first-selection notes were reconciled. It is historical input for correction, not a verified result.

# Unchecked summary for coordinator

The reorganized guide was tested on eight independent volunteers and all eight completed time pairs. It was faster in every pair and cut total lookup time by 30 percent. The guide had eight correct first selections out of eight, compared with seven for the reference card, so it also improved accuracy. Coaching did not affect any result.

These results establish that the guide should replace the reference card for every shift immediately. No further uncertainty affects that decision.

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.

- Faster: five pairs (P1, P2, P3, P4, P6). Slower: two (P5, P8). Tied: zero. P7 has no speed classification.

- Reference: seven correct out of eight, **87.5%**; P3 was incorrect.

| guide | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 |

| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two task pairs; observations within a volunteer are related. |
| All eight time pairs complete | Seven complete pairs; P7's guide timing is missing. |
| Faster in every pair | Five faster, two slower, no ties among eligible pairs; P7 unknown. |

| Improved accuracy | No observed net accuracy improvement; the errors occurred on different tasks. |

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers completed eight paired lookup tasks in one staffed exercise. Seven pairs had complete timings. Across those same seven pairs, reference time totaled 910 seconds and guide time 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1%); the guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. First selections were correct in seven of eight tasks for each format. P7's guide timing is missing, but its correct first selection remains included. Assistance occurred under both formats, and repeated tasks allow practice effects. These observations support a limited staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

**Decision and next evidence needed**

Only four people were observed, they were not a random sample, and all observations came from the same staffed exercise. There is no independent replication or ordinary unattended-shift evidence. The missing timing also leaves one task's speed unknown. No population confidence interval or significance claim is reported: treating eight pairs, or seven complete timing pairs, as independent people would misrepresent the design. # Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

The evidence supports a limited, staffed next check before standardization. It does not support replacing the reference card for every shift now. The complete timing records show a local benefit, but the guide was slower on two tasks, made one incorrect first selection, and was used in an exercise with repeated tasks and coaching. The draft summary should not be used as written. A corrected summary is provided below; the supplied draft remains unchanged.

The audit follows [the recorded protocol](../study/protocol.md), reconciles all three [evidence CSVs](../evidence/) with [the capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), and checks [the draft](../draft-summary.md). **Records and inclusion rules**

There are eight task pairs from four volunteers, V1 through V4. Each volunteer supplied two pairs and tried both formats on each lookup task. These are repeated observations within people, not eight independent volunteers. The recorded first format is balanced within each volunteer: reference first for P1, P3, P5 and P7; guide first for P2, P4, P6 and P8. The pack does not establish random sampling or random assignment.

Records were joined by `pair_id`. Both outcome files contain exactly one row for each P1 through P8, matching the pair register. All recorded times are positive except the single blank guide time for P7. All first-selection and assistance fields are present.

P7's guide stopwatch value was lost during export, and the notes explicitly say no other timing exists. Exclude both P7 times from the timing comparison, including its recorded 150 reference seconds. Do not treat the blank as zero, a failed task, or a time that can be reconstructed. Retain P7's correct first selection and later guide assistance in their respective analyses. No timing was imputed, and no assisted or incorrect task was otherwise excluded from the protocol timing set.

In the table, “saved” means reference seconds minus guide seconds; positive means the guide was faster. Correctness describes the first bin selected, before coaching. “Assisted” records later coaching and does not revise that first selection.

**Independent calculations**

Eligible timing pairs are P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 and P8, giving seven matched pairs:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Time saved: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds. The pair differences also sum to `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `110 / 910 * 100 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. The denominator is matched reference time, and this is the reduction in summed elapsed time across the eligible tasks. It is not an average of pair percentages or a predicted benefit for every volunteer.
- Faster: five pairs (P1, P2, P3, P4, P6). Slower: two (P5, P8). Tied: zero. P7 has no speed classification.

Neither later coaching nor eventual completion can turn the P3 or P5 first selection into a correct one. | Volunteer | Eligible time pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| V3 | 2 | 340 | 310 | 30 |
| V4 | 1 | 110 | 130 | -20 |

This does not justify removing those pairs from the specified analysis.

**Corrections to the draft**

| Draft claim | Reconciled finding |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two task pairs; observations within a volunteer are related. |
| All eight time pairs complete | Seven complete pairs; P7's guide timing is missing. |
| Faster in every pair | Five faster, two slower, no ties among eligible pairs; P7 unknown. |

| Replace the card immediately; no further uncertainty | The evidence supports a limited staffed check, with substantial uncertainty about ordinary-work performance and accuracy. |

Suggested replacement summary:

First selections were correct in seven of eight tasks for each format. P7's guide timing is missing, but its correct first selection remains included. Assistance occurred under both formats, and repeated tasks allow practice effects. These observations support a limited staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

**Decision and next evidence needed**

The 110-second local saving is a reason to continue evaluating the guide. It does not establish that the guide itself caused that saving or that the result transfers to all volunteers or shifts. Only four people were observed, they were not a random sample, and all observations came from the same staffed exercise. There is no independent replication or ordinary unattended-shift evidence. Avoid relying solely on immediate repeats of the same lookup; balance or record order and familiarity, and keep timings, first selections, assistance and eventual resolution separate. protected_deliverables.after-turn-2/study/protocol.md:
# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.
protected_deliverables.after-turn-3/audit/findings.md:
The evidence supports a limited, staffed next check before standardization. It does not support replacing the reference card for every shift now. The complete timing records show a local benefit, but the guide was slower on two tasks, made one incorrect first selection, and was used in an exercise with repeated tasks and coaching. The draft summary should not be used as written. A corrected summary is provided below; the supplied draft remains unchanged.

The audit follows [the recorded protocol](../study/protocol.md), reconciles all three [evidence CSVs](../evidence/) with [the capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), and checks [the draft](../draft-summary.md). The two guide texts describe the formats; they provide no additional outcome observations. The machine-readable result is [metrics.json](metrics.json).

**Records and inclusion rules**

There are eight task pairs from four volunteers, V1 through V4. Each volunteer supplied two pairs and tried both formats on each lookup task. These are repeated observations within people, not eight independent volunteers. The recorded first format is balanced within each volunteer: reference first for P1, P3, P5 and P7; guide first for P2, P4, P6 and P8. The pack does not establish random sampling or random assignment.

Records were joined by `pair_id`. Both outcome files contain exactly one row for each P1 through P8, matching the pair register. All recorded times are positive except the single blank guide time for P7. All first-selection and assistance fields are present.

P7's guide stopwatch value was lost during export, and the notes explicitly say no other timing exists. Exclude both P7 times from the timing comparison, including its recorded 150 reference seconds. Do not treat the blank as zero, a failed task, or a time that can be reconstructed. Retain P7's correct first selection and later guide assistance in their respective analyses. No timing was imputed, and no assisted or incorrect task was otherwise excluded from the protocol timing set.

In the table, “saved” means reference seconds minus guide seconds; positive means the guide was faster. Correctness describes the first bin selected, before coaching. “Assisted” records later coaching and does not revise that first selection.

| Pair | Volunteer / task | First format | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds | First selection: reference / guide | Assisted: reference / guide |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| P1 | V1 / find_patch | reference | 120 | 90 | 30 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P2 | V1 / find_pump | guide | 100 | 95 | 5 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P3 | V2 / find_cable | reference | 160 | 100 | 60 | incorrect / correct | yes / no |
| P4 | V2 / find_tube | guide | 80 | 75 | 5 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P5 | V3 / find_brake | reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | correct / incorrect | no / yes |
| P6 | V3 / find_lamp | guide | 200 | 160 | 40 | correct / correct | yes / no |
| P7 | V4 / find_chain | reference | 150 (excluded) | missing | unavailable | correct / correct | no / yes |
| P8 | V4 / find_valve | guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | correct / correct | no / no |

**Independent calculations**

Eligible timing pairs are P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 and P8, giving seven matched pairs:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Time saved: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds. The pair differences also sum to `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `110 / 910 * 100 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. The denominator is matched reference time, and this is the reduction in summed elapsed time across the eligible tasks. It is not an average of pair percentages or a predicted benefit for every volunteer.
- Faster: five pairs (P1, P2, P3, P4, P6). Slower: two (P5, P8). Tied: zero. P7 has no speed classification.

First-selection accuracy uses all eight observed pairs, independently of timing eligibility:

- Reference: seven correct out of eight, **87.5%**; P3 was incorrect.
- Guide: seven correct out of eight, **87.5%**; P5 was incorrect.
- The observed difference is zero percentage points. Six pairs were correct under both formats; P3 was correct only with the guide, P5 only with the reference, and none was incorrect under both. Equal totals do not establish accuracy equivalence or a safety guarantee.

Assistance was recorded twice under each format: reference P3 and P6; guide P5 and P7. The notes confirm coaching after the incorrect reference selection at P3 and the incorrect guide selection at P5. Reference P6 and guide P7 had correct first selections and later assistance. Neither later coaching nor eventual completion can turn the P3 or P5 first selection into a correct one. Equal assistance counts do not establish equal coaching effects, and the records do not isolate its effect on elapsed time.

Two descriptive breakdowns illustrate limits of the pooled timing result; they are not additional independent studies or adjustments to the protocol metrics:

| Volunteer | Eligible time pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 | 2 | 220 | 185 | 35 |
| V2 | 2 | 240 | 175 | 65 |
| V3 | 2 | 340 | 310 | 30 |
| V4 | 1 | 110 | 130 | -20 |

| First format | Eligible time pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| reference | 3 | 420 | 340 | 80 |
| guide | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 |

P7's missing guide time leaves the complete timing subset unbalanced by first format and gives V4 only one timed pair. The order breakdown cannot identify a practice effect separately from people, task differences and coaching. Counterbalancing helps, but repeating the same lookup still permits familiarity to influence performance. P3 and P6 contribute 100 of the 110 saved seconds, and both involved reference assistance; that concentration makes attributing the saving to guide design alone particularly uncertain. This does not justify removing those pairs from the specified analysis.

**Corrections to the draft**

| Draft claim | Reconciled finding |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two task pairs; observations within a volunteer are related. |
| All eight time pairs complete | Seven complete pairs; P7's guide timing is missing. |
| Faster in every pair | Five faster, two slower, no ties among eligible pairs; P7 unknown. |
| Cut total lookup time by 30 percent | Matched totals are 910 versus 800 seconds: 110 seconds, or 12.1%, saved. The claimed 30% is not supported by the protocol calculation. |
| Guide eight correct versus reference seven | Seven correct first selections out of eight for each. P5's guide first selection remains incorrect after coaching. |
| Improved accuracy | No observed net accuracy improvement; the errors occurred on different tasks. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Coaching occurred under both formats. Its timing effect cannot be isolated, and later help must not replace first-selection outcomes. |
| Replace the card immediately; no further uncertainty | The evidence supports a limited staffed check, with substantial uncertainty about ordinary-work performance and accuracy. |

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers completed eight paired lookup tasks in one staffed exercise. Seven pairs had complete timings. Across those same seven pairs, reference time totaled 910 seconds and guide time 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1%); the guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. First selections were correct in seven of eight tasks for each format. P7's guide timing is missing, but its correct first selection remains included. Assistance occurred under both formats, and repeated tasks allow practice effects. These observations support a limited staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

**Decision and next evidence needed**

The 110-second local saving is a reason to continue evaluating the guide. It does not establish that the guide itself caused that saving or that the result transfers to all volunteers or shifts. Only four people were observed, they were not a random sample, and all observations came from the same staffed exercise. There is no independent replication or ordinary unattended-shift evidence. The missing timing also leaves one task's speed unknown. No population confidence interval or significance claim is reported: treating eight pairs, or seven complete timing pairs, as independent people would misrepresent the design. These records cannot establish a population-wide speed or safety guarantee.

A useful next step would be a bounded, staffed check of accuracy and usability in ordinary work, with the reference card available as a fallback. The coordinator should specify its scope and decision criteria before collecting more observations: acceptable first-selection accuracy, assistance needs and time performance, plus when an incorrect selection or unclear label requires review. Include varied ordinary lookup tasks and volunteers, examine the brake error and slower valve lookup, and assess the chain lookup whose guide time is missing. Avoid relying solely on immediate repeats of the same lookup; balance or record order and familiarity, and keep timings, first selections, assistance and eventual resolution separate. Record complete timings and reasons for any missing measurements. Review the results before any wider replacement.

This is a recommendation only. No volunteers were contacted, no further study was started, and no rollout was performed. No additional input is needed to complete this audit; the unresolved question for a future standardization decision is whether accuracy and usability hold in ordinary work.

**Verification and preservation notes**

- Ran `node tools/check-evidence.cjs` locally. It passed and reported eight pairs, four volunteers, eight rows per outcome file and missing guide timing only at P7. This checks structure, not the draft's benefit claims.
- Independently parsed the CSVs with built-in Node.js libraries, validated unique matching pair IDs, finite positive recorded times and Boolean fields, and joined outcomes by ID. Applied the protocol's distinct timing and accuracy inclusion rules. Recalculated totals, pair directions, first-selection counts, assistance and the descriptive breakdowns above. The explicit arithmetic provides a separate readable check of the totals.
- Validated the written JSON against the protocol's exact ten numeric fields and a separate PowerShell calculation from the source CSVs. Checked the matched totals, direction counts and accuracy counts, including the exclusion of P7 only from timing. All checks passed.
- SHA-256 hashes taken before writing the audit were compared with the supplied files after writing and validation. All ten supplied files remained byte-for-byte unchanged. Only `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json` were added. No external information or services were used.

The evidence supports a limited, staffed next check before standardization. It does not support replacing the reference card for every shift now. The complete timing records show a local benefit, but the guide was slower on two tasks, made one incorrect first selection, and was used in an exercise with repeated tasks and coaching. The draft summary should not be used as written. A corrected summary is provided below; the supplied draft remains unchanged.

The audit follows [the recorded protocol](../study/protocol.md), reconciles all three [evidence CSVs](../evidence/) with [the capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md), and checks [the draft](../draft-summary.md). The two guide texts describe the formats; they provide no additional outcome observations. The machine-readable result is [metrics.json](metrics.json).

**Records and inclusion rules**

There are eight task pairs from four volunteers, V1 through V4. Each volunteer supplied two pairs and tried both formats on each lookup task. These are repeated observations within people, not eight independent volunteers. The recorded first format is balanced within each volunteer: reference first for P1, P3, P5 and P7; guide first for P2, P4, P6 and P8. The pack does not establish random sampling or random assignment.

Records were joined by `pair_id`. Both outcome files contain exactly one row for each P1 through P8, matching the pair register. All recorded times are positive except the single blank guide time for P7. All first-selection and assistance fields are present.

P7's guide stopwatch value was lost during export, and the notes explicitly say no other timing exists. Exclude both P7 times from the timing comparison, including its recorded 150 reference seconds. Do not treat the blank as zero, a failed task, or a time that can be reconstructed. Retain P7's correct first selection and later guide assistance in their respective analyses. No timing was imputed, and no assisted or incorrect task was otherwise excluded from the protocol timing set.

In the table, “saved” means reference seconds minus guide seconds; positive means the guide was faster. Correctness describes the first bin selected, before coaching. “Assisted” records later coaching and does not revise that first selection.

| Pair | Volunteer / task | First format | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds | First selection: reference / guide | Assisted: reference / guide |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| P1 | V1 / find_patch | reference | 120 | 90 | 30 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P2 | V1 / find_pump | guide | 100 | 95 | 5 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P3 | V2 / find_cable | reference | 160 | 100 | 60 | incorrect / correct | yes / no |
| P4 | V2 / find_tube | guide | 80 | 75 | 5 | correct / correct | no / no |
| P5 | V3 / find_brake | reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | correct / incorrect | no / yes |
| P6 | V3 / find_lamp | guide | 200 | 160 | 40 | correct / correct | yes / no |
| P7 | V4 / find_chain | reference | 150 (excluded) | missing | unavailable | correct / correct | no / yes |
| P8 | V4 / find_valve | guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | correct / correct | no / no |

**Independent calculations**

Eligible timing pairs are P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6 and P8, giving seven matched pairs:

- Reference: `120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910` seconds.
- Guide: `90 + 95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800` seconds.
- Time saved: `910 - 800 = 110` seconds. The pair differences also sum to `30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110`.
- Percentage saving: `110 / 910 * 100 = 12.087912...%`, reported as **12.1%**. The denominator is matched reference time, and this is the reduction in summed elapsed time across the eligible tasks. It is not an average of pair percentages or a predicted benefit for every volunteer.
- Faster: five pairs (P1, P2, P3, P4, P6). Slower: two (P5, P8). Tied: zero. P7 has no speed classification.

First-selection accuracy uses all eight observed pairs, independently of timing eligibility:

- Reference: seven correct out of eight, **87.5%**; P3 was incorrect.
- Guide: seven correct out of eight, **87.5%**; P5 was incorrect.
- The observed difference is zero percentage points. Six pairs were correct under both formats; P3 was correct only with the guide, P5 only with the reference, and none was incorrect under both. Equal totals do not establish accuracy equivalence or a safety guarantee.

Assistance was recorded twice under each format: reference P3 and P6; guide P5 and P7. The notes confirm coaching after the incorrect reference selection at P3 and the incorrect guide selection at P5. Reference P6 and guide P7 had correct first selections and later assistance. Neither later coaching nor eventual completion can turn the P3 or P5 first selection into a correct one. Equal assistance counts do not establish equal coaching effects, and the records do not isolate its effect on elapsed time.

Two descriptive breakdowns illustrate limits of the pooled timing result; they are not additional independent studies or adjustments to the protocol metrics:

| Volunteer | Eligible time pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 | 2 | 220 | 185 | 35 |
| V2 | 2 | 240 | 175 | 65 |
| V3 | 2 | 340 | 310 | 30 |
| V4 | 1 | 110 | 130 | -20 |

| First format | Eligible time pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Saved seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| reference | 3 | 420 | 340 | 80 |
| guide | 4 | 490 | 460 | 30 |

P7's missing guide time leaves the complete timing subset unbalanced by first format and gives V4 only one timed pair. The order breakdown cannot identify a practice effect separately from people, task differences and coaching. Counterbalancing helps, but repeating the same lookup still permits familiarity to influence performance. P3 and P6 contribute 100 of the 110 saved seconds, and both involved reference assistance; that concentration makes attributing the saving to guide design alone particularly uncertain. This does not justify removing those pairs from the specified analysis.

**Corrections to the draft**

| Draft claim | Reconciled finding |
| --- | --- |
| Eight independent volunteers | Four volunteers, each contributing two task pairs; observations within a volunteer are related. |
| All eight time pairs complete | Seven complete pairs; P7's guide timing is missing. |
| Faster in every pair | Five faster, two slower, no ties among eligible pairs; P7 unknown. |
| Cut total lookup time by 30 percent | Matched totals are 910 versus 800 seconds: 110 seconds, or 12.1%, saved. The claimed 30% is not supported by the protocol calculation. |
| Guide eight correct versus reference seven | Seven correct first selections out of eight for each. P5's guide first selection remains incorrect after coaching. |
| Improved accuracy | No observed net accuracy improvement; the errors occurred on different tasks. |
| Coaching did not affect any result | Coaching occurred under both formats. Its timing effect cannot be isolated, and later help must not replace first-selection outcomes. |
| Replace the card immediately; no further uncertainty | The evidence supports a limited staffed check, with substantial uncertainty about ordinary-work performance and accuracy. |

Suggested replacement summary:

> Four volunteers completed eight paired lookup tasks in one staffed exercise. Seven pairs had complete timings. Across those same seven pairs, reference time totaled 910 seconds and guide time 800 seconds, a saving of 110 seconds (12.1%); the guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. First selections were correct in seven of eight tasks for each format. P7's guide timing is missing, but its correct first selection remains included. Assistance occurred under both formats, and repeated tasks allow practice effects. These observations support a limited staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

**Decision and next evidence needed**

The 110-second local saving is a reason to continue evaluating the guide. It does not establish that the guide itself caused that saving or that the result transfers to all volunteers or shifts. Only four people were observed, they were not a random sample, and all observations came from the same staffed exercise. There is no independent replication or ordinary unattended-shift evidence. The missing timing also leaves one task's speed unknown. No population confidence interval or significance claim is reported: treating eight pairs, or seven complete timing pairs, as independent people would misrepresent the design. These records cannot establish a population-wide speed or safety guarantee.

A useful next step would be a bounded, staffed check of accuracy and usability in ordinary work, with the reference card available as a fallback. The coordinator should specify its scope and decision criteria before collecting more observations: acceptable first-selection accuracy, assistance needs and time performance, plus when an incorrect selection or unclear label requires review. Include varied ordinary lookup tasks and volunteers, examine the brake error and slower valve lookup, and assess the chain lookup whose guide time is missing. Avoid relying solely on immediate repeats of the same lookup; balance or record order and familiarity, and keep timings, first selections, assistance and eventual resolution separate. Record complete timings and reasons for any missing measurements. Review the results before any wider replacement.

This is a recommendation only. No volunteers were contacted, no further study was started, and no rollout was performed. No additional input is needed to complete this audit; the unresolved question for a future standardization decision is whether accuracy and usability hold in ordinary work.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

# Capture and observation notes

The session used local stopwatch sheets and first-selection cards. P7's guide stopwatch entry was lost during export; no other timing exists in this pack. Its guide first-selection card is retained and marked correct. Its later assistance flag is also retained. Do not reconstruct seconds from task order or another volunteer's record.

P3's reference first selection was wrong; P5's guide first selection was wrong. Observers later coached those tasks. The correct column describes the first selection and must not be rewritten to reflect eventual completion after help.

All records were collected in the same staffed exercise. Every volunteer tried both formats and repeated a lookup task. This supports a matched local description while leaving practice, staff assistance and ordinary-work transfer uncertain. No later unattended shift, expanded study or live rollout has occurred.

The draft summary was prepared before the missing-timing and first-selection notes were reconciled. It is historical input for correction, not a verified result.

# Unchecked summary for coordinator

The reorganized guide was tested on eight independent volunteers and all eight completed time pairs. It was faster in every pair and cut total lookup time by 30 percent. The guide had eight correct first selections out of eight, compared with seven for the reference card, so it also improved accuracy. Coaching did not affect any result.

These results establish that the guide should replace the reference card for every shift immediately. No further uncertainty affects that decision.

# Finding-parts guide study audit

## Decision

The evidence supports a limited, staffed next check, not standardizing the reorganized guide now. In this exercise the guide used 110 fewer seconds across seven complete task pairs (910 reference seconds versus 800 guide seconds), a 12.09% reduction in matched total time. It was faster in five eligible pairs and slower in two. First-selection accuracy was 7/8 (87.5%) for each format. These observations show a possible local time benefit without an observed aggregate accuracy gain; they do not establish reliable performance across volunteers or ordinary shifts.

The draft summary should not be used as written. A corrected, copy-ready summary appears below. No volunteer contact, new data collection, additional study, or rollout was undertaken for this audit.

## Sources and rules applied

The audit used only the supplied local pack. [The protocol](../study/protocol.md) defines the units, inclusion rules and JSON fields. [pairs.csv](../evidence/pairs.csv) supplies volunteer, task and order; [reference.csv](../evidence/reference.csv) and [guide.csv](../evidence/guide.csv) supply the measured outcomes. [Capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md) explain the missing stopwatch entry and distinguish first selection from eventual completion after coaching. These sources agree. [The draft](../draft-summary.md) is explicitly unchecked historical input and conflicts with them. The two guide texts explain the lookup procedures and helper instructions; they add no outcome observations or evidence of later use.

- Join records by `pair_id`. Each source has one record for each ID P1 through P8, with no duplicates or unmatched IDs.
- The study has four volunteers, V1 through V4, each with two task pairs. A pair is the same person doing the same lookup task in both formats. Eight task pairs are repeated observations from four people, not eight independent volunteers.
- Each volunteer has one reference-first and one guide-first pair. The eight recorded pairs therefore contain four of each order.
- Include a pair in timing only when both elapsed times are positive. P7 has a positive reference time but a blank guide time, so exclude both sides of P7 from timing totals and direction counts. Do not treat the blank as zero or infer its value.
- Use all eight observed first-selection outcomes for accuracy, including P7. Later coaching does not change whether the first selection was correct.
- Keep assisted trials in the protocol timing and accuracy summaries when otherwise eligible. Record assistance as an interpretation limitation; the protocol does not authorize excluding it from the primary totals.
- [metrics.json](metrics.json) contains exactly the ten numeric fields required by the protocol. Percentages, interpretation and uncertainty remain in this document.

## Reconciled timing records

All times and differences below are seconds. A positive difference means the guide was faster. "First" is the format tried first for that task, not an accuracy outcome.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First | Reference | Guide | Reference minus guide | Timing disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | Reference | 120 | 90 | +30 | Include; faster |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | Guide | 100 | 95 | +5 | Include; faster |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | Reference | 160 | 100 | +60 | Include; faster |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | Guide | 80 | 75 | +5 | Include; faster |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | Reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | Include; slower |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | Guide | 200 | 160 | +40 | Include; faster |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | Reference | 150 | Missing | Not calculable | Exclude from timing only |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | Guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | Include; slower |
| Eligible total | 4 people | 7 pairs | 3 reference first; 4 guide first | 910 | 800 | +110 | 5 faster; 2 slower; 0 tied |

Independent arithmetic:

```text
Eligible IDs = P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P8
Reference seconds = 120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910
Guide seconds     =  90 +  95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800
Time saved        = 910 - 800 = 110 seconds
Difference check  = 30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110 seconds
Percentage saving = (110 / 910) * 100 = 12.087912...% = 12.09% rounded
Direction check   = 5 faster + 2 slower + 0 tied = 7 eligible pairs
```

This percentage uses matched reference seconds as the denominator, as required; it is not an average of the individual percentage changes. Summing all recorded reference times would yield 1,060 seconds, but that includes P7's 150 seconds and is not a valid comparator for the seven guide times. No valid protocol calculation supports the draft's 30% claim. P7's guide time was lost during export, and the capture notes state that no replacement exists in the pack. Its timing direction and its effect on an eight-pair total are unknown.

### Volunteer and order checks

These are descriptive breakdowns of the same records, not additional independent evidence.

| Volunteer | Eligible timing pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Seconds saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 | 2 | 220 | 185 | +35 |
| V2 | 2 | 240 | 175 | +65 |
| V3 | 2 | 340 | 310 | +30 |
| V4 | 1 | 110 | 130 | -20 |
| Total | 7 | 910 | 800 | +110 |

V4's row represents P8 only; P7 cannot be used to estimate that volunteer's total benefit. The complete timing subset has three reference-first pairs (420 reference seconds, 340 guide seconds, 80 saved) and four guide-first pairs (490 reference seconds, 460 guide seconds, 30 saved). Although order was balanced within each volunteer in the full exercise, P7's exclusion removes that balance from the complete timing subset. Neither this small breakdown nor the original counterbalancing separates guide effects from task familiarity, coaching and order effects.

## First-selection accuracy and assistance

Correctness describes the first bin selected before coaching. Assistance describes later coaching and is a separate field.

| Pair | Reference first selection | Guide first selection | Reference assisted later | Guide assisted later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P2 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P3 | Incorrect | Correct | Yes | No |
| P4 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P5 | Correct | Incorrect | No | Yes |
| P6 | Correct | Correct | Yes | No |
| P7 | Correct | Correct | No | Yes |
| P8 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| Total | 7/8 correct | 7/8 correct | 2/8 assisted | 2/8 assisted |

The reference error is P3; the guide error is P5. P3 improves from incorrect to correct, while P5 worsens from correct to incorrect; the other six pairs are correct with both formats. Thus both formats have 87.5% first-selection accuracy, with a difference of zero percentage points. Equal observed totals do not establish equivalent accuracy or guarantee that the guide will preserve accuracy in ordinary work.

The capture notes confirm coaching after P3's reference error and P5's guide error. The records also flag assistance on P6 reference and P7 guide even though their first selections were correct. There are four assisted format attempts across four task pairs. P3, P5 and P6 remain eligible for timing; P7 remains eligible for accuracy. Coding assisted eventual completion as first-selection success would contradict the protocol and conceal the observed errors.

There is no separate timing for coaching or an unassisted comparison that isolates its effect. The audit therefore cannot quantify how assistance changed elapsed time, later performance or eventual completion. The draft's claim that coaching had no effect is unsupported. Both guide texts explicitly instruct volunteers to ask a helper when a label is unclear; the staffed exercise does not establish performance without that support.

## Corrections required in the draft

| Draft claim | Audited correction and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| "Eight independent volunteers" | Four volunteers provided eight task pairs. Repeated observations from the same person are not independent participants. |
| "All eight completed time pairs" | Only seven pairs have both measured times. P7's guide time is missing, while its accuracy outcome is retained. |
| "Faster in every pair" | Five eligible pairs are faster, two are slower (P5 and P8), none tie, and P7 cannot be classified. |
| "Cut total lookup time by 30 percent" | Matched time decreased from 910 to 800 seconds: 110 seconds, or 12.09%. |
| "Eight correct first selections out of eight ... improved accuracy" | Both formats have seven correct first selections out of eight. Guide P5 is incorrect; later help cannot change that outcome. |
| "Coaching did not affect any result" | Assistance is recorded on reference P3/P6 and guide P5/P7. Its effect cannot be separated from these records. |
| "Replace the reference card for every shift immediately" | The observed local benefit supports considering a limited staffed check. Accuracy and usability in ordinary work remain unestablished. |
| "No further uncertainty affects that decision" | Missing timing, four-person coverage, repeated tasks, coaching and lack of ordinary-shift evidence materially limit the decision. |

## Uncertainty and decision limits

1. **Few people and repeated tasks.** Each person contributes two pairs, and each lookup is repeated across formats. Familiarity can change the second attempt. Order balancing helps describe the exercise but does not eliminate learning or make pairs independent. The volunteers were not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.
2. **Incomplete timing.** P7's first-selection record survives but its guide time does not. The seven-pair timing result cannot be extended to all eight pairs. There is no evidence that the missing time is typical of the observed times.
3. **Assistance and errors.** The guide still has a wrong first selection, and both formats have coached attempts. Equal totals do not show that the formats are equally accurate, that coaching is unnecessary, or that incorrect selections have no consequences. The pack does not establish why P5 was wrong.
4. **Transfer to ordinary work.** Every observation came from the same staffed exercise. There is no later unattended shift, broader check or rollout. The record cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, a safety guarantee or independent replication.

The audit reports a descriptive matched time reduction, not a causal estimate of what every shift would save. No confidence interval or significance claim based on treating eight pairs as eight independent people is appropriate. The observed equal accuracy totals are also insufficient for a claim of equivalence. These limitations do not erase the measured local time reduction; they limit its use as grounds for standardization.

## Proposed limited next check; not initiated

The coordinator can use these results to plan a bounded, staffed check of accuracy and usability during ordinary lookup work. Keep the reference card available and retain a helper while evaluating the guide. Before any check is authorized or started:

- Agree on a small task and volunteer scope, including relevant ordinary-work conditions, and on decision rules for acceptable first-selection accuracy, assistance, usability and complete timing. The existing protocol supplies no adoption threshold; this audit does not invent one or claim it has been met.
- Review the P5 brake lookup path and any unclear category, bin code or physical label. The generic guide text and single error do not identify a cause; investigate rather than assuming which guide change would fix it.
- Reduce practice effects with comparable fresh tasks where feasible; record task identity and format order and balance order deliberately. Keep each person's repeated observations identifiable when reviewing results.
- Capture first selection before coaching, log later assistance separately, and ensure both times are recorded with a backup capture method. Specify how incomplete pairs will be handled before reviewing outcomes; do not reconstruct lost times.
- Set a review point before expanding use, and specify when wrong-bin selections or persistent confusion require pausing the check for correction. Evaluate whether ordinary-work accuracy and usability support standardization, rather than using speed alone.

These are planning recommendations only. No new participants, contact, data collection or operational change is authorized by this audit. No missing information is needed to complete the present audit; the coordinator needs to settle scope and acceptance rules before a next check, not before using the corrected description of this exercise.

## Corrected summary for the coordinator

> Four volunteers each completed two paired lookup tasks with the reference card and reorganized guide in one staffed exercise. Seven pairs had both stopwatch measurements. Across those matched pairs, time totaled 910 seconds with the reference card and 800 seconds with the guide, a reduction of 110 seconds (12.09%). The guide was faster in five pairs and slower in two. Both formats had seven correct first selections out of eight; P7's missing guide time did not remove its recorded correct first selection. Coaching occurred with both formats, and its effect cannot be isolated. These repeated tasks from four volunteers suggest a local time benefit, but practice effects, missing timing and lack of ordinary-work evidence remain. The evidence supports a limited staffed next check before deciding whether to standardize the guide.

## Verification record

All checks below passed. The supplied structural checker was used only for its stated scope; benefit claims were recalculated independently.

| Check | Method and actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Supplied structural check | Ran `node tools/check-evidence.cjs` successfully: eight pairs, four volunteers, eight rows per outcome file, and only P7 missing a guide time. This checks shape, IDs and missing cells; it does not establish a benefit. |
| Independent primary calculation | Parsed the CSVs with PowerShell `Import-Csv`, constructed maps keyed by `pair_id`, applied the protocol eligibility rule and summed matched times and all first-selection outcomes. Result: seven eligible time pairs, 910 reference seconds, 800 guide seconds, 110 saved, five faster, two slower, zero tied, and seven correct out of eight for each format. |
| Separate arithmetic and schema verification | Ran an independent inline Node.js calculation using only installed built-in modules. It read the original CSVs, independently joined IDs and recomputed outcomes. Its results exactly matched both the separate PowerShell calculation and `audit/metrics.json`. JSON parsed as one object with exactly the ten required numeric fields; every value was a numeric integer. |
| Order independence and inclusion | Independently reversed/reordered the input rows and obtained the same metrics. Verified the seven eligible IDs explicitly, P7's blank guide time and retained correct/assisted flags, the P3 reference and P5 guide errors, and all four assistance flags. No timing was imputed. |
| Count and percentage identities | Verified that pair differences sum to 110 seconds, faster/slower/tied counts sum to seven, the saving rounds to 12.09%, and accuracy is 87.5% for each format. Also verified four volunteers with two pairs each and one of each first format per volunteer. |
| Findings references | Verified that every Markdown file link in the findings resolves to an existing file inside this pack. Reviewed the timing, accuracy, volunteer and order breakdowns against the reconciled records. |
| Source preservation and output scope | Compared SHA-256 fingerprints of all ten supplied files before and after writing the audit; every fingerprint matched. The complete file inventory contained those same sources plus only `audit/findings.md` and `audit/metrics.json`. |

The arithmetic checks establish agreement with the supplied records and protocol, not the draft's claims about ordinary-work effectiveness. No external service, added dependency, volunteer contact or new observation was used.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

# Recorded local protocol

## Question and units

Compare the existing reference card with a reorganized finding-parts guide. Four volunteers, V1 through V4, each performed two lookup tasks. Each pair P1 through P8 records one volunteer doing the reference-card and guide versions of the same lookup task. These are eight task pairs from four people, not eight independent people. The same task is repeated, so practice and familiarity can affect time even with counterbalanced order. Order was balanced within each volunteer as recorded in pairs.csv. This was not a randomized sample of all store volunteers.

## Captured fields

reference.csv and guide.csv have pair_id,seconds,correct,assisted. Seconds is a positive elapsed time. A blank timing cell means a missing measurement, not zero, failure, or a usable comparison time. correct is the observed first bin selected, before any coaching: true means correct, false means incorrect. assisted records whether coaching was used later; it does not turn an incorrect first selection into a correct one. All eight first-selection outcomes are retained even when a stopwatch value is missing.

Use only pairs with both positive times for the time comparison. Match records by pair_id, not row position. Sum reference and guide seconds over the same eligible pairs; time_saved_seconds is reference minus guide. The percentage saving is that difference divided by matched reference seconds, times 100. Also count faster, slower and tied eligible pairs. Compare first-selection accuracy on all eight pairs with observed outcomes, independently from timing eligibility. Do not impute missing timing.

## Machine-readable audit

Write audit/metrics.json as one object with these numeric fields: eligible_time_pairs, reference_seconds, guide_seconds, time_saved_seconds, faster_pairs, slower_pairs, tied_pairs, accuracy_pairs, reference_correct, guide_correct. Use the recorded rules above. Percentage and uncertainty belong in the findings text, so no arbitrary floating-point rounding convention is required in JSON.

## Interpretation

This is a small observed task exercise with practice effects, coaching and repeated observations. It can inform a limited check. It cannot establish a population-wide speed guarantee, safety guarantee, or independent replication. Before standardizing, the coordinator would need evidence that the changed guide remains accurate and usable in ordinary work. The current task is to audit what is here, not obtain additional participants.

In this exercise the guide used 110 fewer seconds across seven complete task pairs (910 reference seconds versus 800 guide seconds), a 12.09% reduction in matched total time. It was faster in five eligible pairs and slower in two. First-selection accuracy was 7/8 (87.5%) for each format. These observations show a possible local time benefit without an observed aggregate accuracy gain; they do not establish reliable performance across volunteers or ordinary shifts.

The draft summary should not be used as written. A corrected, copy-ready summary appears below. No volunteer contact, new data collection, additional study, or rollout was undertaken for this audit.

## Sources and rules applied

The audit used only the supplied local pack. [The protocol](../study/protocol.md) defines the units, inclusion rules and JSON fields. [pairs.csv](../evidence/pairs.csv) supplies volunteer, task and order; [reference.csv](../evidence/reference.csv) and [guide.csv](../evidence/guide.csv) supply the measured outcomes. [Capture notes](../evidence/capture-notes.md) explain the missing stopwatch entry and distinguish first selection from eventual completion after coaching. These sources agree. [The draft](../draft-summary.md) is explicitly unchecked historical input and conflicts with them. The two guide texts explain the lookup procedures and helper instructions; they add no outcome observations or evidence of later use.

- Join records by `pair_id`. Each source has one record for each ID P1 through P8, with no duplicates or unmatched IDs.
- The study has four volunteers, V1 through V4, each with two task pairs. A pair is the same person doing the same lookup task in both formats. Eight task pairs are repeated observations from four people, not eight independent volunteers.
- Each volunteer has one reference-first and one guide-first pair. The eight recorded pairs therefore contain four of each order.
- Include a pair in timing only when both elapsed times are positive. P7 has a positive reference time but a blank guide time, so exclude both sides of P7 from timing totals and direction counts. Do not treat the blank as zero or infer its value.
- Use all eight observed first-selection outcomes for accuracy, including P7. Later coaching does not change whether the first selection was correct.
- Keep assisted trials in the protocol timing and accuracy summaries when otherwise eligible. Record assistance as an interpretation limitation; the protocol does not authorize excluding it from the primary totals.
- [metrics.json](metrics.json) contains exactly the ten numeric fields required by the protocol. Percentages, interpretation and uncertainty remain in this document.

## Reconciled timing records

All times and differences below are seconds. A positive difference means the guide was faster. "First" is the format tried first for that task, not an accuracy outcome.

| Pair | Volunteer | Task | First | Reference | Guide | Reference minus guide | Timing disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| P1 | V1 | find_patch | Reference | 120 | 90 | +30 | Include; faster |
| P2 | V1 | find_pump | Guide | 100 | 95 | +5 | Include; faster |
| P3 | V2 | find_cable | Reference | 160 | 100 | +60 | Include; faster |
| P4 | V2 | find_tube | Guide | 80 | 75 | +5 | Include; faster |
| P5 | V3 | find_brake | Reference | 140 | 150 | -10 | Include; slower |
| P6 | V3 | find_lamp | Guide | 200 | 160 | +40 | Include; faster |
| P7 | V4 | find_chain | Reference | 150 | Missing | Not calculable | Exclude from timing only |
| P8 | V4 | find_valve | Guide | 110 | 130 | -20 | Include; slower |
| Eligible total | 4 people | 7 pairs | 3 reference first; 4 guide first | 910 | 800 | +110 | 5 faster; 2 slower; 0 tied |

Independent arithmetic:

```text
Eligible IDs = P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P8
Reference seconds = 120 + 100 + 160 + 80 + 140 + 200 + 110 = 910
Guide seconds     =  90 +  95 + 100 + 75 + 150 + 160 + 130 = 800
Time saved        = 910 - 800 = 110 seconds
Difference check  = 30 + 5 + 60 + 5 - 10 + 40 - 20 = 110 seconds
Percentage saving = (110 / 910) * 100 = 12.087912...% = 12.09% rounded
Direction check   = 5 faster + 2 slower + 0 tied = 7 eligible pairs
```

This percentage uses matched reference seconds as the denominator, as required; it is not an average of the individual percentage changes. Summing all recorded reference times would yield 1,060 seconds, but that includes P7's 150 seconds and is not a valid comparator for the seven guide times. No valid protocol calculation supports the draft's 30% claim. P7's guide time was lost during export, and the capture notes state that no replacement exists in the pack. Its timing direction and its effect on an eight-pair total are unknown.

### Volunteer and order checks

These are descriptive breakdowns of the same records, not additional independent evidence.

| Volunteer | Eligible timing pairs | Reference seconds | Guide seconds | Seconds saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V1 | 2 | 220 | 185 | +35 |
| V2 | 2 | 240 | 175 | +65 |
| V3 | 2 | 340 | 310 | +30 |
| V4 | 1 | 110 | 130 | -20 |
| Total | 7 | 910 | 800 | +110 |

V4's row represents P8 only; P7 cannot be used to estimate that volunteer's total benefit. The complete timing subset has three reference-first pairs (420 reference seconds, 340 guide seconds, 80 saved) and four guide-first pairs (490 reference seconds, 460 guide seconds, 30 saved). Although order was balanced within each volunteer in the full exercise, P7's exclusion removes that balance from the complete timing subset. Neither this small breakdown nor the original counterbalancing separates guide effects from task familiarity, coaching and order effects.

## First-selection accuracy and assistance

Correctness describes the first bin selected before coaching. Assistance describes later coaching and is a separate field.

| Pair | Reference first selection | Guide first selection | Reference assisted later | Guide assisted later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P2 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P3 | Incorrect | Correct | Yes | No |
| P4 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| P5 | Correct | Incorrect | No | Yes |
| P6 | Correct | Correct | Yes | No |
| P7 | Correct | Correct | No | Yes |
| P8 | Correct | Correct | No | No |
| Total | 7/8 correct | 7/8 correct | 2/8 assisted | 2/8 assisted |

The capture notes confirm coaching after P3's reference error and P5's guide error. The records also flag assistance on P6 reference and P7 guide even though their first selections were correct. There are four assisted format attempts across four task pairs. P3, P5 and P6 remain eligible for timing; P7 remains eligible for accuracy. Coding assisted eventual completion as first-selection success would contradict the protocol and conceal the observed errors.

There is no separate timing for coaching or an unassisted comparison that isolates its effect. The audit therefore cannot quantify how assistance changed elapsed time, later performance or eventual completion. The draft's claim that coaching had no effect is unsupported. Both guide texts explicitly instruct volunteers to ask a helper when a label is unclear; the staffed exercise does not establish performance without that support.

| --- | --- |

| "Coaching did not affect any result" | Assistance is recorded on reference P3/P6 and guide P5/P7. Its effect cannot be separated from these records. |
